pages: He took his face off in front of us. Not with a knife. He stood at the altar and he let the grey finish what it had started, and we watched the features go - slowly, like a footprint in wet sand. When it was done he put on the mask, and he said: now I cannot be recognised, and now I cannot be lied to, and now nothing that loves me can find me. Some of the novices wept. He let them. He said it would pass.
